title: Adding Animation to Websites
summary: Finishes the drum kit by flashing the pressed drum. A buttonAnimation(key) function finds the matching element by its class, adds a pressed CSS class, and uses setTimeout to remove it after 100 ms.

concepts.heading: Shared animation function
points: Both click and keyboard paths already call makeSound with a single character, so a second function buttonAnimation(currentKey) is called beside it in both places.
Passing the same one-character value to both keeps the two input routes consistent.

concepts.heading: Finding the right button
points: In the HTML each drum button has the shared class drum plus a class equal to its letter (w, a, s, d, j, k, l).
querySelector uses CSS selector syntax, so a class needs a leading dot: document.querySelector(".w").
Because the key is only the bare letter, build the selector by concatenation: "." + currentKey. Store the result in activeButton.
(Extra) A key with no matching element (e.g. "x") makes querySelector return null, and the next line throws a TypeError. Guard with an if (activeButton) check.

concepts.heading: Applying the visual state with classList
points: styles.css already defines .pressed, giving the element a lighter box-shadow and 50% opacity.
Test the idea in the console first: document.querySelector("h1").classList.add("pressed") applies the style immediately.
activeButton.classList.add("pressed") switches the button into its pressed look.
On its own, the class never goes away, so the effect only happens once.

concepts.heading: setTimeout for the reset
points: setTimeout(function, delayInMilliseconds) runs a function once after a delay; it is another callback-taking function.
First argument: the function to run later (an anonymous function here) which calls activeButton.classList.remove("pressed").
Second argument: the delay in ms. 100 ms (0.1 s) was chosen by experimenting; it reads as a quick flash.
The code after setTimeout does not wait; the add runs immediately and the remove fires 100 ms later.
Because the animation lives in the shared function, it works for clicks and keys with no extra code.

task.name: Add the pressed class to the active button
task.starting_point: Drum kit with makeSound working for clicks and keys; styles.css already contains .pressed.
task.goal: When a drum is clicked or its key typed, the drum briefly shows the pressed style, then returns to normal.
steps: Create buttonAnimation(currentKey) and call it next to makeSound in both listeners.
Select the element with document.querySelector("." + currentKey) and store it in activeButton.
Challenge: add the pressed class using classList.add.
Look up setTimeout and use it to remove the class after about 100 ms.
Test with clicks and with each of the seven keys.
task.expected_result: Each drum dims with a small shadow for a tenth of a second whenever triggered.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 18 - Advanced Javascript and DOM Manipulation/18.09 - Adding Animation to Websites/script.js

pitfalls: Forgetting the dot when building the selector (querySelector(currentKey)).
Delay passed in seconds rather than milliseconds.
Calling the remove immediately outside setTimeout, so the class vanishes before painting.
Pressing a non-drum key throws an error because querySelector returns null.

Tasks: add and remove a class manually in the console; build selector from a key; flash after 100 ms; guard against null; try a CSS transition for a smoother fade.
Starter: three pad divs with letters and a .pressed rule.
